title: The House of David
subtitle: The Tel Dan Stele

images.caption: The Tel Dan Stele in the Israel Museum.

p: Pieces of a basalt victory monument, written in Aramaic, most likely set up by Hazael king of Aram-Damascus after he fought the kings of Israel and Judah. The king boasts of killing “[Jo]ram son of [Ahab], king of Israel” and “[Ahaz]iah son of [Joram], king of the House of David”.

The words bytdwd, “House of David”, are the earliest known mention of David outside the Bible, written little more than a century after his reign. The reading is now widely accepted. The account is told from Aram’s perspective. It shows that David was remembered by Israel’s neighbours as the founder of Judah’s royal house, answering scholars who had doubted he was a historical king.
facts: 1993 and 1994, at Tel Dan in northern Israel
